Homespun.Helm: A felt cap, stitched by a mother who wanted it back with you still under it.
Homespun.Hauberk: A shirt of undyed wool, patched at the elbows. Every island makes them, and no two agree on how.
Homespun.Gauntlets: Work gloves worn soft at the palm. Whoever had them last hauled a great deal of rope.
Homespun.Greaves: Breeches and good shoes, the kind a cobbler swears will see you to the end of the road.
Homespun.Sword and Shield: A plain blade and a board of salvaged planking. The paint on the shield was a boat's name once.
Homespun.Dagger and Shield: A gutting knife and a pot lid with a strap riveted on. People have held doorways with less.
Homespun.Twin Daggers: Two net knives from the same bench, one sharper than the other. Nobody remembers which.
Homespun.Sword: Hammered out by a village smith between ploughshares. It has a good edge and no opinions.
Homespun.Twin Swords: A pair the smith made because the first came out short. The second came out short as well.
Homespun.Staff: A length of ash cut for walking. It has done more than walk.
Homespun.Mace: An iron knob on a stick, the sort kept behind a tavern door for closing time.
Homespun.Twin Maces: Two cudgels out of the same chandler's barrel. They were sold for driving pegs, and they still drive them.
Homespun.Mace and Shield: A mallet and a cart's tailboard, carried by a drover who was tired of losing the cart.
Homespun.Great Axe: A felling axe with a longer haft than it needs. The woodsman who made it had stopped cutting trees.
Homespun.Greatsword: Too much iron and too little polish. It was the biggest thing the forge could make that week.
Homespun.Flail: A threshing flail with a nail or two driven through the swingle. The harvest was never the same.
Homespun.Warhammer: A quarry hammer, one face worn smooth from splitting stone.
Homespun.Bow: A hunting bow strung with waxed twine. It has fed a family through more than one winter.
Homespun.Crossbow: A fowler's crossbow, its stock cut with a tick for every goose. The ticks stop halfway down.
Homespun.Pistolet: A plain pistolet with a cracked grip bound in wire. It fires, most days.
Homespun.Brace of Pistolets: Two old pistolets that never matched, bought in one lot at a widow's sale.
Homespun.Thunderlock: A long gun loaded the slow way, down the mouth. It was a ship's before it was anyone's.

Deckhand.Helm: A tarred leather cap that keeps off the spray and the boom. Mostly the boom.
Deckhand.Hauberk: A jerkin cut from an old sea-chest's hide and hardened with salt and sweat. Deckhands sleep in them.
Deckhand.Gauntlets: Leather mitts scored by a thousand turns of line. The palms are harder than the hands.
Deckhand.Greaves: Leggings laced tight below the knee, so nothing catches when the deck heels over.

Smuggler.Helm: A hood with a deep brim, for faces that would rather not be remembered on the quay.
Smuggler.Hauberk: Its lining has more pockets than a harbourmaster has questions, and some are very well hidden.
Smuggler.Gauntlets: Thin gloves for counting coin in the dark and leaving no print on the crate.
Smuggler.Greaves: Soft-soled and dark to the hip, for wading ashore at low tide with something heavy.

Shoreguard.Helm: An open helm with a brim to shade the eyes, for watching a beach all day for a sail that might be the Grey Tithe's.
Shoreguard.Hauberk: Rings over quilting, rusted at the collar where the salt gets in. The shore watch never has time to scour it.
Shoreguard.Gauntlets: Mail gauntlets with a hook stitched at the thumb, for hauling the drowned up the shingle.
Shoreguard.Greaves: Mail to the knee, then good boots. A shoreguard walks the tideline at every change of watch.

Portwatch.Helm: The port watch's helm, with a lantern bracket at the brow. In the stories the bracket is always empty.
Portwatch.Hauberk: Plates riveted over leather and stamped with the watch's mark. A night on the quay in one is a long night.
Portwatch.Gauntlets: Heavy enough to hold a gangway shut against a crew that has decided to come ashore anyway.
Portwatch.Greaves: They clank on the cobbles, and the watch likes it that way. Thieves hear them coming, and choose.
Portwatch.Sword and Shield: The watch's blade and its round shield, painted in the harbour's colours. The paint always wears off the left side first.
Portwatch.Dagger and Shield: A long knife and a buckler for the alleys behind the fish market, where a sword has no room.
Portwatch.Twin Daggers: Two blades from the watch's armoury, issued to whoever is sent down into the holds to look.
Portwatch.Sword: A watchman's sword, plain and heavy, its scabbard worn white where it rubbed the harbour wall.
Portwatch.Twin Swords: Two short swords for the night watch on the piers, where you never know which side it will come from.
Portwatch.Staff: The watch's long staff, shod in iron at both ends, for ending a fight without starting another.
Portwatch.Mace: Issued to the watch for drunk sailors. It has met a few who were not drunk.
Portwatch.Twin Maces: A pair of the watch's batons, iron-headed, for when one baton was not making the point.
Portwatch.Mace and Shield: A watch-sergeant's kit. The shield has a slot to see through; the mace has no need of one.
Portwatch.Great Axe: Kept in the watchhouse for cutting mooring lines when a ship must not leave. It is rarely used on lines.
Portwatch.Greatsword: It hung over the watchhouse door until the night the door came in. It has been carried since.
Portwatch.Flail: A chain and weight the port watch took off a pressgang, and kept.
Portwatch.Warhammer: Made for knocking the pins out of a gangway. The watch found it knocks other things out as well.
Portwatch.Bow: A watchtower bow. Its archer could put a fire arrow into a hull at the harbour mouth.
Portwatch.Crossbow: Racked loaded by every watchhouse window, so the watch never has to hurry.
Portwatch.Pistolet: A watchman's pistolet, fired more often into the air than at anyone. Not always, though.
Portwatch.Brace of Pistolets: Two pistolets on one belt, for a watchman who walks the quay alone.
Portwatch.Thunderlock: The long gun on the watchtower's sill. One shot from it brings every lantern in the port alight.

Wayfarer.Helm: A helm with a traveller's scarf wound round it. Every road it has walked has left its dust in the weave.
Wayfarer.Hauberk: Made to be worn for weeks between ports where no smith will mend it.
Wayfarer.Gauntlets: Their knuckles are scratched with the names of ports, one for every landfall. Some of the names are crossed out.
Wayfarer.Greaves: They have kept pace on every road and gangway, and asked for nothing but oil.
Wayfarer.Sword and Shield: A traveller's blade, and a shield with a map scratched inside it that matches no coast.
Wayfarer.Dagger and Shield: Carried by a courier who rode the island roads with letters no one else was to read.
Wayfarer.Twin Daggers: Two blades a wayfarer bought in two ports, which turned out to carry the same maker's mark.
Wayfarer.Sword: A good sword, the kind a traveller buys once and is buried with.
Wayfarer.Twin Swords: A pair for the long roads: one for the road ahead, and one for whatever follows.
Wayfarer.Staff: A pilgrim's staff notched once for every crossing. It has run out of room.
Wayfarer.Mace: Short enough to hang from a saddle, heavy enough to end an ambush.
Wayfarer.Twin Maces: Two flanged maces for a long road with bad company on it.
Wayfarer.Mace and Shield: A caravan guard's pair. The shield is dented by arrows that came out of the hedges.
Wayfarer.Great Axe: Taken on the roads to clear a fallen tree, or whoever felled it across the way.
Wayfarer.Greatsword: Carried on a shoulder from port to port, by someone no captain ever refused passage twice.
Wayfarer.Flail: A traveller's flail that folds into a pack, and unfolds faster than a highwayman expects.
Wayfarer.Warhammer: A hammer that has knocked on a great many doors after dark. They opened, in the end.
Wayfarer.Bow: Unstrung on the march and strung in a breath, for roads where game and trouble keep the same paths.
Wayfarer.Crossbow: Its stirrup is worn bright from being wound at every crossroads.
Wayfarer.Pistolet: Kept under a coat on the long roads. It has crossed more water than its owner.
Wayfarer.Brace of Pistolets: Two pistolets for a coach roof, one for each side of the road.
Wayfarer.Thunderlock: A long gun wrapped in oilcloth, carried from one port to the next and fired only at the end of each.

Barrowknight.Helm: Taken from a barrow where the knight inside still wore it. The cheek-guards had been closed from the inside.
Barrowknight.Hauberk: A knight's coat of plates from a barrow, its surcoat long rotted. The dents in it are older than the island's records.
Barrowknight.Gauntlets: Found folded over a sword's hilt in a barrow, as if the hands had only just let go.
Barrowknight.Greaves: The barrow's knight was buried standing, and these are why he stayed up.

Gravewarden.Helm: Worn by those who kept the barrows' doors. It has eye-slits at the back as well as the front.
Gravewarden.Hauberk: A grave-keeper's coat, as bright as the day it was buried. Nothing in the barrows tarnishes it.
Gravewarden.Gauntlets: The wardens wore these to carry the dead in. The fingers stay cold, whatever the weather.
Gravewarden.Greaves: Their soles are worn on the inside edge, as if the wardens walked in circles round something.
Gravewarden.Sword and Shield: A warden's sword, and the shield they set flat on the barrow's stone. Nothing has lifted the stone since.
Gravewarden.Dagger and Shield: For the narrow passages under the barrows, where a warden fought on their knees.
Gravewarden.Twin Daggers: A warden's two knives: one for the living who came to rob the dead, one for the dead who would not stay.
Gravewarden.Sword: Kept bright by the barrow wardens, who believed the dead could see their own faces in it.
Gravewarden.Twin Swords: Two blades crossed on a warden's tomb lid. They were the only thing in the barrow that had been moved.
Gravewarden.Staff: Topped with a bell that does not ring. The wardens said it rang underground.
Gravewarden.Mace: Its head is wound with grave-wire. The wardens used it on what climbed out.
Gravewarden.Twin Maces: The wardens beat these on the barrow doors at dusk, so whatever was inside knew they were awake.
Gravewarden.Mace and Shield: A gatewarden's pair from a barrow mouth, the shield scored by something with long nails.
Gravewarden.Great Axe: It hung over a barrow's inner door, its edge turned to the dark and not the way in.
Gravewarden.Greatsword: The last warden's blade, found driven point down into a barrow's floor like a grave marker.
Gravewarden.Flail: A censer chain weighted for war. The wardens swung it through the barrows to keep the air moving, they said.
Gravewarden.Warhammer: For driving the grave-pins home. Some of the pins were found pulled out again.
Gravewarden.Bow: Its arrows are fletched in grey, and they fly quietly, so as not to wake anyone.
Gravewarden.Crossbow: Set over a barrow's door to cover the way out, not the way in.
Gravewarden.Pistolet: Found in a barrow that was sealed before anyone on the island had heard a shot.
Gravewarden.Brace of Pistolets: Two pistolets left on a barrow's altar, primed and loaded, for whoever came next.
Gravewarden.Thunderlock: The wardens' long gun, its barrel engraved with names. The newest one is still blank.

Wreckborn.Helm: Hammered from a ship's bell that came up in a net. It still rings in a high wind.
Wreckborn.Hauberk: Plate beaten from a wreck's iron knees, still curved like the hull it held together.
Wreckborn.Gauntlets: Spiked at the knuckle with ship's nails. The one who wore them never let go of a rope, or a throat.
Wreckborn.Greaves: Cut from a wreck's rudder fittings. They are heavy, and they steer.
Wreckborn.Sword and Shield: The shield is a ship's hatch and the blade its bosun's. Both came up out of the same wreck, in an Elite Dungeon's dark.
Wreckborn.Dagger and Shield: A rigging knife and a porthole's iron cover. The glass is gone; the bolts are not.
Wreckborn.Twin Daggers: Two marlinspikes ground to blades by a crew that had nothing else left to fight with.
Wreckborn.Sword: A cutlass from a wreck's armoury, its basket hilt furred with rust and still sound.
Wreckborn.Twin Swords: A boarding pair from a wreck, found crossed on the captain's door as if to keep someone in.
Wreckborn.Staff: A broken spar shod in iron, carried by whoever led the wreck's crew after the captain fell.
Wreckborn.Mace: A capstan's iron cap on a stave, made by a crew that had been at sea too long to remember land.
Wreckborn.Twin Maces: Two belaying pins weighted with shot. A wreck's crew settled every quarrel with them.
Wreckborn.Mace and Shield: A deadeye on a haft and a round of deck planking. Somebody made a life aboard that wreck.
Wreckborn.Great Axe: A wreck's fire-axe, its edge notched from cutting away its own masts in a storm.
Wreckborn.Greatsword: Forged from a wreck's keel-bolt by someone who wanted a blade as long as their grudge.
Wreckborn.Flail: A length of anchor chain with the shackle still on the end. It came up from below, and so did whoever swings it.
Wreckborn.Warhammer: A shipwright's maul with caulking still in the head. It has opened hulls and closed arguments.
Wreckborn.Bow: Its limbs were cut from a wreck's gunwale and it is strung with tarred line. It still smells of the hold.
Wreckborn.Crossbow: A deck crossbow sawn off its swivel and carried down into the dark.
Wreckborn.Pistolet: Salvaged dry from a wreck that sank in a calm. Nobody can explain the calm, or the dry powder.
Wreckborn.Brace of Pistolets: Two pistolets taken off the same drowned officer. The water had not reached his collar.
Wreckborn.Thunderlock: A wreck's swivel gun cut down to carry. It kicks like the deck it was bolted to.

Brightwater.Helm: Pale as shallow water over sand. Those who wore it said it let them see further.
Brightwater.Hauberk: So light the wearer forgets it until a blade finds it. Then the blade remembers.
Brightwater.Gauntlets: They catch the light like a flat calm, and whoever stares at them looks away first.
Brightwater.Greaves: Worn by someone who crossed the shallows at a run and never once looked down.
Brightwater.Sword and Shield: The shield is polished like still water, and an attacker sees themselves in it, a little late.
Brightwater.Dagger and Shield: A bright knife and a shield as thin as a shell. An Elite Dungeon's captain carried them where the water let the light in.
Brightwater.Twin Daggers: Two blades as pale as the shallows: hard to see in a hand, and harder to see coming.
Brightwater.Sword: A blade so bright it looks wet. Light runs along it the way water runs off an oar.
Brightwater.Twin Swords: A pair that flash like sun on the swell. Their owner chose to fight facing west, at evening.
Brightwater.Staff: A pale staff that holds a little daylight after dark: enough to read by, and no more.
Brightwater.Mace: Its head is fluted like a shell, and as light. It hits like a breaker.
Brightwater.Twin Maces: Two bright maces that ring like glass when they meet each other, and like bells when they meet anything else.
Brightwater.Mace and Shield: Carried by someone who guarded a well in an Elite Dungeon's depths. The well was dry.
Brightwater.Great Axe: Its blade is a crescent as thin as a gull's wing, and harder than the rocks gulls drop shells on.
Brightwater.Greatsword: A long blade that weighs less than it should. Those who carry it walk a little lighter too.
Brightwater.Flail: A bright ball on a fine chain. In the dark it looks like a lantern swinging.
Brightwater.Warhammer: It leaves no dent where it strikes, only cracks, and then nothing.
Brightwater.Bow: A pale bow that never warps in the wet. Its archer stood in the surf to shoot.
Brightwater.Crossbow: It draws so light a child could wind it, and its bolts still go through a door.
Brightwater.Pistolet: Its pan is polished like a mirror. Its owner checked their teeth in it.
Brightwater.Brace of Pistolets: Two pale pistolets that flash before they fire, so there is a breath to regret things.
Brightwater.Thunderlock: A long bright gun that stays cool in the hand, even after the shot.

Deepwarden.Helm: Its visor is a single slit, cut for eyes long used to the dark of the deep.
Deepwarden.Hauberk: Heavy enough to drown anyone. The Deepwardens were never expecting to come back up.
Deepwarden.Gauntlets: Forged to keep a grip at the bottom of an Abyss Dungeon, where nothing should still be holding on.
Deepwarden.Greaves: The Deepwardens walked the Abyss floor in these, and whatever lived there learned the sound.
Deepwarden.Sword and Shield: The shield is a hatch from a deep door, still locked. The sword is the key, the wardens said.
Deepwarden.Dagger and Shield: A short blade and a heavy shield for the Abyss's lowest stair, where the wardens held for longer than anyone counted.
Deepwarden.Twin Daggers: Two blades worn thin by honing in the dark, where a warden had nothing else to do.
Deepwarden.Sword: A blade that never rusts, kept by a warden of the deep who could not remember the colour of the sky.
Deepwarden.Twin Swords: Carried by a warden who fought with their back to the deep door: one blade for each side of it.
Deepwarden.Staff: As dense as stone. It sinks in water, and seems to drag the light down with it.
Deepwarden.Mace: It falls faster than it should. The wardens dropped it down shafts to hear how deep they went.
Deepwarden.Twin Maces: Their hafts are wound with the line a warden used to find the way back up.
Deepwarden.Mace and Shield: The wardens of a deep door held it with these. The scratches on the shield are on the inside.
Deepwarden.Great Axe: Made to cut through the dark, and whatever came up out of it.
Deepwarden.Greatsword: Heavier than any arm should lift. The warden who carried it is said to have grown into it.
Deepwarden.Flail: A heavy ball on a short chain, swung in the wardens' dark like a pendulum counting time.
Deepwarden.Warhammer: Made to drive back whatever presses at the Abyss's lowest door.
Deepwarden.Bow: A heavy bow drawn by a warden who could hear their arrows land, far below.
Deepwarden.Crossbow: Wound by a crank as thick as a wrist. Its bolts were made to stop something the wardens never named.
Deepwarden.Pistolet: Sealed against the damp of the deep. It fires under water, once.
Deepwarden.Brace of Pistolets: Two pistolets as heavy as anchors, carried by a warden who liked to be sure.
Deepwarden.Thunderlock: The wardens fired it down the Abyss stairs, and counted the echoes.

Blackwater.Helm: As black as the water past the reef at night. Those who wore it were seen only by their breath.
Blackwater.Hauberk: It holds no reflection at all. Lanterns held near it seem to dim.
Blackwater.Gauntlets: Smooth as a seal's skin and always a little wet, though nothing ever drips from them.
Blackwater.Greaves: They leave wet prints on dry stone, in the shape of a foot that is not quite the wearer's.
Blackwater.Sword and Shield: A sword and shield brought up out of an Abyss Dungeon, the water still running off them.
Blackwater.Dagger and Shield: The shield is round as a porthole, and the knife as long as the hand that drowned holding it.
Blackwater.Twin Daggers: Two blades that do not show in the dark. They are noticed by the cold.
Blackwater.Sword: It comes out of the scabbard wet, and it has not been near the sea since it was found.
Blackwater.Twin Swords: Two blades that whisper like water when they cross.
Blackwater.Staff: As cold to hold as deep water, even by the fire.
Blackwater.Mace: Its head rings like a stone dropped down a well, long after it has stopped.
Blackwater.Twin Maces: Two maces whose heads are beaded with water that never dries.
Blackwater.Mace and Shield: Its shield is dark and smooth, and what looks into it sees the sea at night.
Blackwater.Great Axe: It cuts like a tide coming in: slowly, and then completely.
Blackwater.Greatsword: Found standing upright in an Abyss pool, as if someone below had pushed it up.
Blackwater.Flail: Its chain does not clink. It moves like weed in a current.
Blackwater.Warhammer: It strikes without a sound, like a wave in the dark you only hear afterwards.
Blackwater.Bow: Its arrows hiss as they fly, like rain on dark water.
Blackwater.Crossbow: Its bolts come out of the dark wet, from a crossbow no one sees until it is lowered.
Blackwater.Pistolet: Its flash is the only light it ever gives, and it gives it once.
Blackwater.Brace of Pistolets: Carried by someone who came ashore at night and was not there in the morning.
Blackwater.Thunderlock: Dredged from an Abyss Dungeon's flooded hall, dry inside, and loaded.

Reefborn.Helm: Grown over with coral on the seabed, then cut free. A few polyps still open in the rain.
Reefborn.Hauberk: Its scales overlap like a fish's, and it turns a blade the way a reef turns a keel.
Reefborn.Gauntlets: Ridged like a reef's crest. Whatever grabs them lets go.
Reefborn.Greaves: Made for wading the reef at low tide, where every step lands on an edge.
Reefborn.Sword and Shield: The shield is a great shell and the sword a long tooth set in a grip. A sea dungeon gave up both.
Reefborn.Dagger and Shield: A shell-backed buckler and a knife of sharp spine, from a sea dungeon whose walls were grown, not built.
Reefborn.Twin Daggers: Two blades as slender as eel spines, and they slip into a gap just as well.
Reefborn.Sword: A long blade curved like a wave about to break. Barnacles keep trying to settle on it.
Reefborn.Twin Swords: Two curved blades that move like a pair of fish turning together.
Reefborn.Staff: Cut from a wood that grows on no island anyone knows, and found in a sea dungeon. It is warm, like shallow water at noon.
Reefborn.Mace: Its head is a knot of coral harder than stone. It is still growing, very slowly.
Reefborn.Twin Maces: Two coral-headed maces that have been growing towards each other.
Reefborn.Mace and Shield: A coral mace and a shield of plaited weed gone hard as horn, from a sea dungeon's drowned court.
Reefborn.Great Axe: Its head is shaped like a ray's wing, and it glides through the swing the way a ray glides over sand.
Reefborn.Greatsword: A long, thin blade that sings faintly in the swell, as a reef does on a calm night.
Reefborn.Flail: An urchin's spiked shell on a cord of plaited kelp. Those it hits ache for days.
Reefborn.Warhammer: Headed with a fist of coral. Reefs break hulls; this breaks the rest.
Reefborn.Bow: Strung with sinew from something with fins. It wants the sea, and it shoots towards it.
Reefborn.Crossbow: Its bolts are tipped with shell, and they whistle like wind through the gaps in a reef.
Reefborn.Pistolet: Its barrel is crusted with coral inside and out, and still it fires true.
Reefborn.Brace of Pistolets: Two pistolets grown over together on a sea dungeon's floor, and only lately cut apart.
Reefborn.Thunderlock: Found in a sea dungeon with its stock gone to coral. Nobody knows what it was loaded with.

Brassbound.Helm: Banded in brass like a diving bell. Inside, someone scratched a tally of breaths.
Brassbound.Hauberk: Plate riveted like a ship's boiler. It goes green in the salt and never weakens.
Brassbound.Gauntlets: Hinged brass at every knuckle, made by someone who built the locks for sea doors.
Brassbound.Greaves: Brass-shod and heavy, for walking the floor of a sea dungeon where the water used to be.
Brassbound.Sword and Shield: The shield is a porthole's brass rim, the sword banded to match. Both came out of a flooded sea dungeon's armoury, dry.
Brassbound.Dagger and Shield: A brass-hilted knife and a buckler riveted like a sea door, carried by a sea dungeon's keepers on their rounds.
Brassbound.Twin Daggers: Two brass-collared knives in watertight sheaths. Whoever carried them meant to swim.
Brassbound.Sword: A broad blade with a brass guard gone green. The maker's mark is a ship no list has heard of.
Brassbound.Twin Swords: Two blades from a sea dungeon, numbered on the tang: nine and ten.
Brassbound.Staff: Banded in brass rings like a ship's sounding pole. The marks on it go deeper than any sea near here.
Brassbound.Mace: A mace with a brass valve set in its head. Turn it, and it hisses.
Brassbound.Twin Maces: Cast like ship's fittings, and still stamped with the hold they were meant for.
Brassbound.Mace and Shield: A brass mace and a shield like a hatch, carried by the keeper of a sea dungeon's lock.
Brassbound.Great Axe: Brass bands hold its great head to the haft. It was made to cut a jammed sea door free.
Brassbound.Greatsword: Banded in brass above the guard, so a keeper could hold it short in a sea dungeon's tunnels.
Brassbound.Flail: A brass ball on a chain, like the one that hangs from a sea door's bell-pull. Somebody pulled it too hard.
Brassbound.Warhammer: A riveter's hammer, from whoever built the sea dungeons' doors. The rivets are still holding.
Brassbound.Bow: Brass-capped at the tips and strung with wire. It was made where nothing wooden lasts.
Brassbound.Crossbow: Brass-geared and wound with a key. Its ratchet ticks like a ship's clock.
Brassbound.Pistolet: A brass-barrelled pistolet, its pan sealed with wax against the sea's damp.
Brassbound.Brace of Pistolets: Two brass pistolets that close into one case, like a navigator's instruments.
Brassbound.Thunderlock: A brass long gun with a barrel like a speaking tube. Its report carries under water.

Lattice.Helm: Something grew through it from the inside. Whoever wore it was from one of the ruined ports, and stood very still.
Lattice.Hauberk: It was a dockworker's once. The facets came later, and they are still coming, a little at a time.
Lattice.Gauntlets: The fingers end in points no smith forged. They grew while someone in a ruined port was reaching for something.
Lattice.Greaves: Taken from a ruined port, where they had grown into the cobbles. Prising them up took four people.
Lattice.Sword and Shield: The shield was a harbour's sign and the sword a watchman's, before a Breach got into both and changed them.
Lattice.Dagger and Shield: A fish knife and a cooper's lid from a ruined port, grown hard and many-sided. They hum when held.
Lattice.Twin Daggers: Two shards from a Breach, sharp on every face. They are warm, and they should not be.
Lattice.Sword: It was a sword when it was carried into the Breach. What came out weighs the same, and has more edges.
Lattice.Twin Swords: Two blades from a ruined port that grew from one root. Held apart, they lean towards each other.
Lattice.Staff: A harbour pole from a ruined port, grown through end to end. Light goes in and does not come out where it went in.
Lattice.Mace: Its head grew on a ruined port's bollard by itself. Someone snapped it off and found it made a mace.
Lattice.Twin Maces: Cut from a ruined port's railings. The growth on each is the same shape, facet for facet.
Lattice.Mace and Shield: A port's door and the bar that held it, both overtaken. The door still has its knocker.
Lattice.Great Axe: A woodsman's axe from the ruined ports, its blade grown wider than the iron it started from.
Lattice.Greatsword: A long shard pulled out of a Breach, with a hilt someone made for it after. The hilt is starting to change too.
Lattice.Flail: A chain from a ruined port's quay, every link grown into a jagged knot. It chimes as it swings.
Lattice.Warhammer: A cobbler's hammer from a ruined port that kept its head when its owner did not. Its face is many-sided now.
Lattice.Bow: Its limbs were grown, not carved, and they bend without a sound. The string was all anyone had to add.
Lattice.Crossbow: Its bolts grow back in the groove after each shot, slowly.
Lattice.Pistolet: Its barrel was overtaken. It fires shards that nobody loaded.
Lattice.Brace of Pistolets: Two pistolets from one ruined port's armoury, grown together at the grip and broken apart again.
Lattice.Thunderlock: The long gun of a ruined port's watchtower, grown through and changed. Its shot leaves a thin hum in the air.
